title: Low-degree approximation gives a threshold representation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Set $k=\left\lfloor \frac n2+\frac n2\sqrt{\frac{2\log(48n)}{n}}\right\rfloor$. Suppose there is a real-valued function $q$ on the cube whose Fourier coefficients vanish on every subset of coordinates of size greater than $k$, and such that $|f(x)-q(x)|<1/2$ for every $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Then $f$ is represented by the sign of a real-valued polynomial on the cube whose Fourier degree is at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
Cutoff k is the specified floor expression
Approximant has zero Fourier coefficients outside subsets of size at most k
Uniform approximation error is strictly less than 1/2
